sentences.text: The Facts:-

On 10.01.2013 at about 18.00 hours the driver of the involved bus drove the same along the Mecheda-Digha road towards Digha at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and lost his control and thereby dashed against a truck which was proceeding towards Mecheda near Bikramnagar.
As a result, the deceased and many passengers sustained severe injury and the deceased with some of other passengers died.
The driver of the offending bus bearing No. W.B.-11-A/1064 was fully responsible for such accident.
Hence, the petition for compensation.
3. The O.P. No. 2/Insurance Company contested the case by filing a written statement denying all the material allegation as mentioned in the petition.
The O.P. No. 2 denied the age and income of the deceased as mentioned in the petition.
He also denied the manner, place and style of occurrence of the alleged accident.
He has stated that there was no negligence and rashness on the part of the driver of the alleged offending vehicle.
4. The O.P. No. 1 i.e. owner of the offending vehicle did not contest the case in spite of valid service of notice upon him.
5. Four witnesses were examined by the claimants and relevant documents were proved and marked as Exhibit 1 to 14.
6. No evidence was adduced by the opposite parties.

7. Considering the materials on record, the learned Tribunal held as follows:-
"Now, if the monthly income of the deceased be Rs.6000/-, then the annual income stands as Rs.6000/- X 12 = Rs.72000/-.
After deduction of 1/3rd of personal and living expenses the amount stands as Rs.48000/-.

After applying the multiplier 16,
the amount stands as Rs.48000/- X 16 = Rs.768000/-.
The claimants are also entitled to get Rs.2000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.2500/- towards loss of estate.
The claimant No. 1 is also entitled to get Rs.5000/- towards loss of consortium.
Thus, the total amount stands as Rs.777500/-."

8. Being aggrieved the claimants/appellants have preferred this appeal on the grounds:-
a) That the compensation granted is inadequate and thus not 'Just Compensation'.
b) The Tribunal did not consider compensation under other heads to which the claimants are entitled to under the law.
9.

From the materials and evidence on record, it is evident that:-

Admittedly, the Claimants have received the amount of compensation of Rs. 7,77,500/- together with interest in terms of order of the learned Tribunal.

Accordingly, the claimants are now entitled to the balance amount of compensation of Rs. 3,14,500/- together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till deposit.

12. Taking into consideration the amount already received by the Claimants/Appellants, the Respondent No. 1/ Insurance Company shall deposit the balance amount, along with the interest,
